svg.title: LACF frame layout
svg.desc: The fields of a LACF frame (LoRa APRS Compact Frame, spec 11 draft) and a worked example: a position beacon of 82 bytes as plain text is 35 bytes as a LACF frame and 44 bytes after one relay hop.
svg.text: LoRa APRS Compact Frame, spec 11 draft. A draft in early development; the format may change. Sizes are in bytes.
1. The fields, in the order they are sent
The text of the packet (or the
comment after a position), coded by
PPM. V = protocol and table version,
L = length, CRC-16 over the text and
Dashed boxes are optional. The position block exists only in kinds 1 and 3 (9 B for a plain position; longer with a timestamp, course or altitude).
The RXT block only appears after a relay has added its measurements.
Plain content (header kind 0 or 1) is V, CRC and the text; the encoder uses it when LACF content (V L CRC payload) would not make the frame shorter.

svg.text: N0RLY-1*: the relay's callsign replaces WIDE1-1
RXT block added by the relay: tuple 50 20 45 10, mask 81
plain LoRa APRS text frame: 82 B
LACF frame: 35 B, 57% smaller for this packet (real packets average about 44%)
LACF after one relay hop, with the RXT block: 44 B, against 83 B as text: 47% smaller for this packet
Colours only group the bytes; every group is also named. Frame bytes come from the reference code (tools/hb) and a different packet gives different bytes and sizes.
Spec: spec/11-native-ppm-frame-byte-plan.md. Developed with Fabrice Morel, F4MLV (moricef): his native LoRa APRS frame with K6ATV's PPM compression.
